attributes.authority: a Roadwarden relay; the Salt Assembly keeps a factor's room above the depot
features: the old ferry jetty - cut stone, the only rock for 200 miles
the rock cistern in the island's spine, brackish, unreliable
the hide-roofed depot: rope, spare axles, tallow, salt-fodder
the mooring rings, still bolted to the jetty, used now to tie awnings
attributes.population: ~50 permanent; a hundred more whenever two crossings meet
attributes.position: on the beacon line, 13 days (~250 miles) south of Bell Harrow
attributes.role: the meeting point: northbound and southbound crossings lie up here, so news, mail and contracts change hands here or nowhere
attributes.water: the rock cistern only - brackish, and in a dry season the depot sells it by weight at four times Bell Harrow prices

name: The Dry Ferry
summary: A waystation built on the stone jetty of a drowned island, thirteen days out, where a ferry crossed the Meniscus when the Meniscus was water. The jetty is the only rock on the plain and everything leans on it: a hide-roofed depot, a walled pound, a cistern cut into the island's spine that yields brackish water in a bad year and enough in a good one. It is where crossings meet coming and going, which makes it the plain's only market, its only rumour-mill, and the only place between the rims where a man can be found who did not want to be.
